summary: Iteration 5 — Password login + brute force + return visitor + intro replay + secret info card + konami guard. All 17 backend pytest cases passed (100%). All frontend flows tested via Playwright passed (100%): /login rendering, wrong credentials show login-denied, /adcom-admin unauth redirects to /login, correct login navigates to admin dashboard, admin-signout logs out to /login, secret-info-btn appears after 60s on desktop only (mobile 390px correctly hidden), secret-info-card opens with Konami visual + closes via ×/outside/ESC without dimming page, Konami code guarded inside input fields, Konami outside inputs activates ADAM, sessionStorage intro replay counter 1/2/3 behaves correctly (full intro → skip button → immediate workspace), sessionStorage clear resets to full intro, return visitor banner renders with resume-yes/resume-fresh buttons and prior transcript is restored on resume-yes.

minor.issue: backend/.env has CORS_ORIGINS="*" combined with allow_credentials=True in CORSMiddleware. Per CORS spec, browsers reject Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * when credentials are used. Currently works because same-site preview URL doesn't need CORS, but any future cross-origin admin dashboard call from a different origin would fail. Recommend setting CORS_ORIGINS to explicit frontend origin(s).

action_items: Consider tightening CORS_ORIGINS (currently '*' with allow_credentials=True — invalid per spec, may bite when admin panel is served from a different origin).

SecretInfoButton mounts a 60s timer once on load; if user resizes from desktop to mobile mid-session the button DOM is still created (though CSS `hidden md:block` still hides it). Cosmetic — no user-facing bug.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py password_login: brute-force counter is keyed on `ip:email`. If a legitimate user is behind a NAT and someone else spams their email, both would be locked out. Acceptable for admin bootstrap but worth noting.

auth.py password_login uses `x-forwarded-for` first header entry unstripped of trusted proxies — OK for now given single Kubernetes ingress, but never trust XFF blindly if bypassing ingress becomes possible.

adam_leads.get_lead_by_email trusts URL path — since the endpoint is UNAUTHENTICATED, anyone can enumerate leads by guessing emails. Not a security break for lead-capture app, but noteworthy — consider requiring at least a matching session_id or a lightweight token.
